sources: dossier=node.md Required behaviors ('POST /nodes/{id}/reset is a pure retry-budget clear... clears the failed-terminal row's evaluator state, settling-signal-type, and stale frame_id', 2026-06-16/17 transcript); doc=concepts/node.md:25 (pre-fix) named node-reset as an example of an action mutating rimsky_nodes; code=postgres/nodes.go:396 ResetFailedTerminalSettlingSignalType UPDATEs rimsky_node_runs, not rimsky_nodes; instance-terminate DELETEs rimsky_nodes (postgres/nodes.go:438), it does not UPDATE it either
note: Dossier confirms node-reset operates on the node-run row only; repo-wide grep finds zero UPDATE rimsky_nodes statements, and instance-terminate deletes rather than mutates the row. The invariant's named example was doubly wrong. Fixed node.md to state the row is set once and never updated, deleted only at instance-terminate, and that node-reset never touches it.

sources: dossier=node.md net position ('Message emission is a dedicated node-kind (rimsky.emit_message utility node...)'); doc=concepts/node.md:20 Adjacent list (pre-fix) omitted message-sender-node; code=lib/graph/node/kind_resolver.go CanonicalizeSendMessageSugar carries both @concept: message-sender-node and @concept: node; concepts.md TOC confirms message-sender-node.md exists as a first-class concept
note: message-sender-node is a real node specialization sharing a citation site with node and is listed in the concept catalog TOC; its absence from node.md's Adjacent list was an omission, not a design choice. Added it to the Adjacent list.

sources: dossier=node-run.md Conflicts ('RESOLVED 2026-07-14... aggregation rule table... snapshotted onto the parent run at dispatch, strict default'); doc=concepts/node-run.md:22 (pre-fix) said 'snapshotted from the template-node spec at run creation time'; code=postgres/queue.go:85 and sqlite/queue.go:105 Enqueue omit aggregation_policy from INSERT (defaults NULL); fanout_dispatch.go:138 calls UpdateAggregationPolicy only during a fan-out parent's dispatch
note: The dossier's resolved conflict entry explicitly places the aggregation-policy snapshot at fan-out dispatch time, matching code (populated only for fan-out parents, only at fan-out dispatch, never at row creation). Doc was stale on both the timing and the fan-out-only scope. Fixed.

sources: dossier=node-run.md Boundaries ('Owns:... sequence... columns') and decision:sequence-scope-monotonic (sequence exists for 'the latest-run lookup... and the dispatcher's predecessor probes', never described as driving claim order); doc=concepts/node-run.md:24 (pre-fix) said sequence 'Drives dispatcher claim order (lowest unblocked sequence wins)'; code=postgres/queue.go:187 SelectCandidates ORDER BY d.enqueued_at, d.sequence, d.id (enqueued_at primary, sequence a per-(node,scope) tiebreaker, not a global ordering key)
note: No dossier or decision entry ever attributes global claim-order authority to sequence; decision:sequence-scope-monotonic describes only predecessor-lookup and latest-run-lookup roles, consistent with code's enqueued_at-primary ordering. The doc's claim-order sentence was an overstatement not backed by any intent source. Corrected to describe sequence as a same-instant tiebreaker.

sources: dossier=tag.md (no explicit disambiguation requirement, but terminal-tag is an independently attested distinct concept); doc=concepts/tag.md:20 (pre-fix) Boundaries never named terminal-tag; concepts/terminal-tag.md:20 already states 'Distinct from concept:tag (alias template-tag), which is a movable string alias for a template hash; the two nouns share the word but have no overlap in meaning, scope, or carrier'
note: terminal-tag.md already disambiguates itself from tag one-directionally; tag.md never reciprocated despite the bare overloaded slug. This is a repo-established convention (the terminal-tag doc itself models it), not a contested intent question, so it is corrected as a doc completeness defect rather than left as a design-call.

sources: dossier=tag.md (silent on fan-out ownership) and template.md dossier (template lifecycle, including deploy, is a template-owned entry point); doc=concepts/tag.md:20 (pre-fix) Boundaries 'Owns: ... lifecycle event fan-out'; code=lib/control/controlapi/templates.go handleDeployTemplateState calls FanOutTemplateEvent after ListByTemplate, i.e. the template-deploy handler emits and fans out the event, tags merely ride its payload
note: No intent source assigns fan-out ownership to the tag concept; the emission call site lives structurally in the template-deploy handler. The doc's 'Owns' list overstated tag's role versus the accurate parenthetical already present. Moved fan-out out of tag's Owns list into a Does-NOT-own clarification attributing the event to template.

sources: dossier=template.md net position ('Re-registering the same spec is idempotent'), silent on which layer; doc=concepts/template.md:16 (pre-fix) 'Idempotent re-registration is a persistence-layer property'; code=lib/foundation/persistence/{postgres,sqlite}/templates.go Insert returns shared.ErrTemplateInUse on a duplicate id (a conflict); lib/control/controlapi/templates.go handleDeployTemplate calls GetByHash first and returns 200 without calling Insert when a row already exists
note: Dossier confirms idempotent re-registration is intended behavior but never attributes it to the persistence layer; the persistence layer in fact returns a conflict, and the no-op is implemented in the control-API registration handler. Corrected the layer attribution.

sources: dossier=template.md Intentional absences ('Lifecycle-handler slots... retired entirely 2026-05-23') and ('frame_resolution / frame_resolution_mode and the coalesce frame mode — dropped entirely 2026-06-14'); doc=concepts/template.md:12 (pre-fix) 'What it is' named 'frame-resolution policy, handler declarations, quality rules'; code=lib/foundation/spec/template.go TemplateSpec has no Handler field and no frame-resolution field; rg quality over lib/foundation/spec and lib/graph returns nothing
note: All three named artifacts (frame-resolution policy, handler declarations, quality rules) are retired-or-never-existed per the template dossier's own Intentional absences and Superseded sections. Replaced the enumeration with the template's actual current top-level surfaces (subscriptions/cascade coupling, message schemas, publishers, params schema, late-bind services, sub-graphs), matching TemplateSpec's real fields and closing the omission the finding also flagged.

sources: dossier=atomic-staging.md net position ('the bundled filesystem store deliberately does in-place writes... and advertises sync-only write-semantics') and Intentional absences ('write-semantics permits the sync-only subset'); doc=concepts/atomic-staging.md (pre-fix) Adjacent list omitted write-semantics and Definition never stated the relationship; code=lib/foundation/persistence (staging.go) gates every staging decision on writeSemantics=='staged_async'
note: The atomic-staging dossier itself uses write-semantics vocabulary (staged_async / sync-only) to describe which stores get the pattern, confirming the two concepts are directly coupled by design, not merely by implementation accident. Added a defining sentence plus the Adjacent entry.

sources: dossier=sensor.md (silent on citation form); doc=concepts/sensor.md:34 (pre-fix) 'Inert payload per invariant: message-inertness'; design corpus=concepts/inertness.md:35 registers this invariant as numbered §24 (parenthetically aliased 'message-inertness'); peer doc concepts/message.md:31 cites it as 'invariant: 24'
note: The canonical registry numbers this invariant §24; the numeric form is the citation convention peer docs (message.md) actually use, and per the self-containment rule invariant IDs are the stable citation form. sensor.md's bare-slug citation broke that convention. Corrected to 'invariant: 24'. (publisher.md and publisher-subscription.md carry the identical bare-slug form but are outside this cluster's six docs and were left untouched.)

sources: dossier=node-run.md ('the async-acknowledgement identity is populated when the executor returns an await-callback outcome'; supervisor cluster row 579 finding); decision=uniform-attributes-delta.md ('The mid-dispatch attribute writeback callback that an earlier asymmetric design forced is retired; the run-terminating verdict is the only channel an executor uses to mutate node attributes') and decision=keepalive-endpoint.md ('bumps last_progress_at on the dispatch row'); doc=concepts/node-run.md:13 (pre-fix) 'The progress timestamp is bumped by attribute writeback callbacks and by keepalive notifications'; also node-run.md:15 (pre-fix) described scratch mid-dispatch writes as 'paralleling the executor protocol's incremental attribute-writeback callback', naming the same retired mechanism
note: Confirmed per decision:uniform-attributes-delta: mid-dispatch attribute writeback is retired; attributes only mutate via the run-terminating verdict. The liveness field is bumped only by keepalive and scratch writeback. Fixed both the flagged liveness-field sentence and a second stale reference to the retired attribute-writeback callback found in the same section while fixing it (scratch-recovery mechanics), per the fix-every-bug-you-find rule.
